Ms. Doris Yin’s Speech for the GCV Industry Alliance Philippines Convention🗣️

Theme: Connecting Real Business to the Decentralized Future

Dear Philippines GCV Industry Alliance Special Envoys, GCV Ambassadors, Pi Network/GCV warriors, business owners, merchants, and pioneers,
Good afternoon. 
Today, I am deeply honored to join you all at this historic GCV Industry Alliance Convention here at the Gensan View Hotel in General Santos City, Philippines 🇵🇭.

First, let me extend my heartfelt appreciation to the incredible leaders of the Philippines GCV community—those who have carried this movement with strength, courage, and unshakable spirit:

Mr. Marlon Domantay – Education Ambassador 
Mr. Anthony Nierra – Ecosystem Development Ambassador 
Mrs. Lerma Ablan – Merchant Coordinator  
Mr. Julio Villarosa – Merchant Coordinator 
Mr. Jomar Gallego – Merchant Coordinator 
Mr. Jerwin Figueroa – Chair of the GCV Industry Alliance 
Ms. Marivic Temblador – Pi Network General and Warrior Mr. Arnel Reyes – Kawit Cavite Ambassador and Sunday Tribune Owner/Publisher 
Ms. Frelyn Sajor – Region 4A Ambassador 
Mr. Alcher Tejero Capin – Region 2 Regional Ambassador

Most importantly, I want to give special recognition to Ms. Lumari Founder of the Philippines GCV Movement, Head of the Philippines GCV Ambassadors, Global GCV Core Team Executive Director, and International GCV Industry Alliance Chair. 

In 2023, when the world was still unfamiliar with GCV, when doubt and hesitation were common—Ms. Lumari courageously launched GCV Barter in the Philippines. Her sacrifice, vision, and unwavering dedication laid the foundation for what we see today. For that, we are forever grateful.

To all Industry Alliance Special Envoys, regional ambassadors, municipal ambassadors, and brave GCV warriors—you are the shield and voice of this movement. And to all the pioneers and merchants in the Philippines: thank you from my heart ❤️.

Your collective effort has generated over 3.8 million GCV data points. This is a testament to your discipline, belief, unstoppable determination, selfless sacrifice, and tireless efforts.

Even when few believed in GCV in August 2023, you stood firm. You endured the sun and rain. You pushed forward despite laughter, doubt, or misunderstanding. You lead among all global pioneers and turn GCV into reality. You sparked the first flame. And your courage turned that flame into a global fire.

Let me be clear: our journey is not over. We move forward—stronger, wiser, and more united—as we approach DEX activation and GCV activation. Each sacrifice will be meaningful. Every step will be rewarded. Together, we will build something unprecedented.

Today, we are joined by an extraordinary assembly:  
All Philippines GCV Ambassadors  
GCV Industry Alliance Special Envoys 
Industry Alliance chairs and vice-chairs 
Merchants, entrepreneurs, and business owners from across the country

And international speakers from Vietnam, the Arab Region, China, and Africa GCV Industry Alliance Chairs

We are also honored by the presence of Ms. Lumari and Mr. Jojo as guest speakers—thank you for your inspiring contributions to this convention.

What Is the Meaning of the GCV Industry Alliance?

Today, I want to discuss the true essence of the GCV Industry Alliance—because this Alliance is not just an organization; it is a gateway to the future.

The long-term success of Pi Network depends not only on technology but also on real-world integration. This is where the Industry Alliance plays a vital role.

You are the bridge
between real businesses
and the decentralized Web3 blockchain economy.

You are the guides
who will introduce Pi Network to enterprises, communities, and ordinary people.

You are the ones helping local businesses find their new home—
a place where small enterprises can thrive,
where ordinary people can rise together,
and where wealth is accessible to many, not just a few.

In my view, the world of business is one big village. We are connected—economically, socially, and spiritually.

Pi Network embodies tolerance, unity, and integrity—values that enable former competitors to become partners and grow together.

This vision is why I love Pi Network.
It empowers real people.
It boosts small businesses.
It creates prosperity, not through competition, but through collaboration.
This is the decentralized future we are building—
and the Philippines stands at the forefront.
Conclusion

To all pioneers, leaders, and business partners here today:
Your role matters.
Your contribution matters.
Your belief has already moved mountains—and it will move even more.
God bless the Philippines.

Thank you for your strength, unity, and unwavering commitment to GCV.

Together, we march toward the Open Mainnet and a new economic era.

Thank you!
Doris Yin
Founder, Global GCV Movement

Japan-China Spat: Where Does this Leave PH Under a Scandal-Driven Marcos Presidency?
Anna Malindog-Uy
Headsight
The Manila Times
November 22, 2025

WHEN great powers squabble, small states pay the price. And in today’s Asia, the spat is no longer a polite diplomatic dance. It’s an increasingly public, sharp-edged confrontation between Japan and China. Japan’s new prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, with the swagger of someone who forgets the historical lessons and caveats of World War II, declared that Japan may intervene militarily if China “takes over” Taiwan in a way that threatens Japan’s survival and collapses its “pacifist ambiguity” and violates the spirit, if not the text of Article 9 of Japan’s post-war Constitution that renounces war and prohibits the threat or use of force as a means of settling international disputes. In many more ways than one, the statement of Takaichi effectively pre-authorizes war, which is constitutionally problematic and politically and regionally destabilizing. Note that Japan has long relied on strategic ambiguity to maintain deterrence without explicitly committing to war.

Furthermore, Takaichi has basically locked Japan into a more rigid position and removed diplomatic ambiguity. Her politicization of Japan’s foreign policy for domestic favor, for political signaling, rallying conservative support, and projecting leadership strength is problematic because the domestic political theater is being played out at the expense of international military risks, while Japan’s neighbors, specifically China, see this as populist warmongering. Such poorly calibrated statements in a high-risk environment fuel the security dilemma.

Of course, Beijing, unsurprisingly, replied with fire and fury, travel warnings, summons of diplomats, stepped-up coast guard patrols, and PLA drones buzzing around the Senkaku/Diaoyu islands as if to say: “We, too, can raise the temperature.”

But while Tokyo and Beijing exchange diplomatic artillery, Southeast Asia, particularly the Philippines, sits on the geopolitical fault line. And unlike Japan’s well-coordinated national security apparatus or China’s monolithic strategic machinery and state-of-the-art military capability, the Philippines today is led by a president whose government is drowning in massive corruption scandals, with deeply securitized US-leaning foreign policy, with the more entrenched Japan-US-Philippines trilateral defense/military alliance anchored on the RAA (Reciprocal Access Agreement), a president who, according to his older sister, is a drug-dependent, facing the broadest calls for resignation since the Estrada era. Indeed, the universe is yelling right now: “Change leadership before the geopolitical storm hits.”
